text:
Dillon Boucher got his first NHL call-up at 29, and the Chicago Tribune wrote about it, including his first NHL fight, which he called a pretty special moment. He went undrafted and worked his way up through the AHL.

The NHL part so far is five games, about eight minutes a night, no points and 12 hits. Scott Powers of The Athletic noted he played 2:16 in the first period against Columbus on Nov 19 and then took a penalty 38 seconds into the second. That's the life of a call-up.

At five on five Chicago has been about even in expected goals with him on, in a very small sample. His last AHL season was eight points in 53 games for Rockford, so nobody is expecting offense.

What to watch: whether he stays with the Blackhawks once their injured forwards return. Either way, the story of a 29-year-old getting his first NHL game is the kind of thing that makes a long season worth it.
